SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

# Project Kestrel: Seller Draft Review Against Buyer Playbook

**Preliminary notes**
- The Seller's "key negotiated positions" are assertions, not agreed terms. Nothing here is cleared or final.
- The Seller's 20% / AUD 4.8m cap and 18-month period match our conditional fallbacks. Neither fallback is authorised: the cap needs Amelia Frost's prior written authority identifying the draft, and the 18-month period needs her written approval. Neither has been given.
- Disclosure Letter facts are stated as at 22 September 2026. Today is 5 November 2026, so the status of Bluefen, Riverlark, the bonuses, the incident and the Sandbar renewals must be refreshed before we rely on them.

---

**SPA-N-001: General liability cap**
- **Seller:** 20% of price (AUD 4,800,000) for general Warranty Claims.
- **Buyer should want:** 25% (AUD 6,000,000) starting position. The 20% fallback is available only with Frost's written authority.
- **Recommendation:** Reject 20% and hold at 25%. Escalate to Frost only if the fallback is needed, because the number matching our fallback does not clear it.

**SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket**
- **Seller:** AUD 25,000 de minimis; AUD 250,000 basket with recovery of the excess only (deductible).
- **Buyer should want:** AUD 5,000 de minimis; AUD 50,000 aggregate basket with the Seller liable from the first dollar once exceeded.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Both thresholds are materially worse than our position, and the deductible structure is not acceptable.

**SPA-N-003: General claims time limit**
- **Seller:** 18 months after Completion, and a blanket rule that any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.
- **Buyer should want:** 24 months after Completion. The 18-month fallback needs Frost's written approval. The blanket rule must be removed.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the blanket rule. Hold at 24 months; 18 months is not authorised.

**SPA-N-004: Fundamental / Title regime**
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties.
- **Buyer should want:** A separate regime with a 100% cap, at least six years, and outside the general basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Merging title into the general regime is not acceptable for administrative convenience.

**SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out**
- **Seller:** Clauses 9.3, 12.8 and 20.5 apply limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance to "all Claims of any nature." No fraud carve-out is shown.
- **Buyer should want:** Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. No one may waive this.
- **Recommendation:** Reject and insert the carve-out expressly. As drafted, the Seller's language would catch fraud claims.

**SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope**
- **Seller:** General disclosure of the whole data room (DD-002 to DD-012), the Accounts, statutory registers and public records (Disclosure Letter 1.1 and 1.2).
- **Buyer should want:** Specific fair disclosure only. Reject whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- **Recommendation:** Reject 1.1 and 1.2 in full. General disclosure would cut across every specific warranty.

**SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier**
- **Seller:** Clause 8.3 bars claims for any matter the Buyer or its advisers knew of, including anything discoverable from the data room or public records.
- **Buyer should want:** Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions deleted. Any qualifier must name Seller knowledge persons and require reasonable enquiry, and must never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- **Recommendation:** Delete clause 8.3. A discoverable-from-data-room test would wipe out most of our claims.

**SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent**
- **Seller:** Reasonable endeavours; consent treated as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent. The Disclosure Letter (item 2) confirms no final consent and no evidence that the conditions in clause 11.3 are met. Bluefen is about AUD 3.6m of FY26 revenue (about 30%).
- **Buyer should want:** Effective consent and evidence that its conditions are satisfied before Completion. Reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a material customer consent.
- **Recommendation:** Reject consent-on-delivery and reasonable endeavours. Make it a condition precedent with evidence.

**SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility**
- **Seller:** Approximately AUD 3.2m outstanding, to be addressed by a release provided after Completion. The Disclosure Letter (item 3) confirms the facility is unpaid and no discharge is included.
- **Buyer should want:** Current payout figure, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective security releases. Any post-Completion release requires an irrevocable undertaking and Frost's approval.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the post-Completion release. Require payout at Completion, with a refreshed payout letter.

**SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses**
- **Seller:** The AUD 420,000 bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and are not itemised in the funds flow. The Disclosure Letter (item 5) notes payroll tax and on-costs are not addressed.
- **Buyer should want:** The AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs as a specific funds-flow line item or Seller-funded. The funds flow must not silently exclude them.
- **Recommendation:** Require a specific line item or Seller funding, including on-costs. The "matter for the Seller" wording does not resolve the exposure.

**SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity**
- **Seller:** The indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment and is "considered adequate." The AUD 180,000 open balance is not independently verified.
- **Buyer should want:** A broadened indemnity that preserves the SOW3 cure. The AUD 180,000 must be verified independently, not taken from the Seller or the data room.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the narrow indemnity. Broaden it and obtain independent verification of the payment position and the clause 7.3 transfer condition.

**SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident (DD-006)**
- **Seller:** A "preliminary operational matter" not expected to be material.
- **Buyer should want:** Logs preserved, the incident investigated, and regular updates required. Assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand, in either direction. The Disclosure Letter describes about 1,240 records that may be affected.
- **Recommendation:** Do not accept "not material." Require preservation, investigation and updates, and assess whether a specific indemnity is needed. Do not characterise the matter as a confirmed breach.

**SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000)**
- **Seller:** Ordinary-course operating costs.
- **Buyer should want:** Assessment of whether each renewal is unavoidable, terminable or accrued. No automatic Debt classification and no automatic price deduction.
- **Recommendation:** Assess before accepting the ordinary-course characterisation. Do not deduct from price or classify as Debt at this stage.

**SPA-N-014: Category separation**
- **Seller:** Clauses 9.3, 12.8 and 20.5 apply one regime across all Claims, and the Tax/IP positions are "settled under the general regime."
- **Buyer should want:** Title, Tax, IP, payment and covenant categories kept separate, with no hidden general-regime override.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Restore separate categories and remove the blanket override.

**SPA-N-015: Title verification**
- **Seller:** Title is "evidenced by" the share register at DD-012.
- **Buyer should want:** Independent title, ownership, encumbrance and authority evidence. DD-012 is a supplied internal source, not independent proof.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Commission independent searches (for example, company and security registers) and treat DD-012 as a supporting document only.

**SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms**
- **Seller:** Tax and IP warranty positions are "settled under the general regime."
- **Buyer should want:** Tax and IP terms kept open. Assume no unlimited liability and no resolution.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the "settled" characterisation. Keep these items open and out of the general regime's caps and time limits, pending separate negotiation.

---

**Next steps**
1. Refresh the status of Bluefen, Riverlark, the bonuses, the incident and the Sandbar renewals as at today's date.
2. Escalate to Amelia Frost only if we want to consider the 20% cap or 18-month fallbacks. Her written authority, identifying the draft, is needed first.
3. Prepare a mark-up that reverses the Seller's positions on SPA-N-001 to SPA-N-016, starting from our baseline.
